entities.summary: The Book of Obadiah is a canonical biblical text within the Old Testament, attributed to Obadiah, a prophetic figure from the Assyrian period. Written circa 550 BCE, this text contains prophetic declarations against the Edomites, Philistines, and other nations, offering a message of judgment and redemption. Its significance lies in its role as a source of Jewish identity and its influence on Christian theology, particularly in the development of the New Testament's eschatological narrative. The Book of Obadiah has also been studied for its insights into the cultural and political dynamics of the ancient Near East, particularly during the 7th century BCE. This text's historical importance stems from its enduring relevance in the Jewish and Christian traditions, as well as its continued study by scholars of ancient Near Eastern history and literature.
